newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cocoa demand ebbs in Germany after bargain hunt.
newsitem.headline: Cocoa demand ebbs in Germany after bargain hunt.

text.p: Cash cocoa buyers in Germany have disappeared after taking advantage of a post-election slide in sterling last week, traders said on Wednesday.
European consumers made some purchases for the second half of 1997 and the first quarter of 1998 when sterling went below 2.80 marks.
Traders said the industry had signalled buying interest at favourable sterling levels and below basis 1,000 stg on July futures in London, which was last up 15 stg at 1,004.
Purchasing departments appeared to have no money to waste because operating margins in the chocolate industry were down.
"Chocolate sales are unsatisfactory...some companies I talk to have reported sales declines by 10 percent in 1997," one trader in Hamburg said.
Elsewhere, traders shrugged off cocoa futures gains on currency-related buying in the United States.
"I think this will be soon overruled by bearish crop fundamentals," one said, citing last week's spate of crop estimates supporting lower deficits than previously thought.
Cocoa butter demand was flat although the butter ratio over futures had fallen by some 15 points over the last six weeks.
The ratio was at 2.40 spot, 2.45 for the third quarter and 2.53 for the fourth quarter.
Implied mark prices liquid ex-works were 6.78 marks May/June, 6.96 marks for the third quarter and 7.02 for the fourth.
West African beans were quoted at 2.74 marks/kg cif for 1997 shipment dates, compared with 2.70-2.75 marks a week ago.
Recent trades had been done at around 2.65-2.70.
Sterling was at 2.8113 marks at the Frankfurt exchange fixing at midday.
